title: Pointing fits predict large responses at five selected KIC 11084727 dips in six tests but require extrapolation
abstract: We test a pointing explanation for eight selected aperture-flux dips of KIC 11084727 in Kepler release 25. We fit linear and quadratic functions of the reported image motion outside all event windows. We use three running-mean baseline lengths. For five dips, the predicted response is more than half the measured response in all six tests. For the known comet-like dip, the predicted fraction is 1.7 to 7.3 percent. The main five-day quadratic fits have positive validation skill outside events. However, the five large event predictions have maximum design leverage 16 to 56 times the training maximum. Thus, the pointing explanation requires extrapolation in the filtered predictors. Coefficient resampling does not measure that error. These results identify a testable instrument model, but do not establish a cause or a new astronomical source. No independent telescope data are used. We preserve code, source paths and hashes, fixed event selections, all model responses, validation results, figures, and a retrieval recipe.
